solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

definitions.note: British slang: pants means rubbish, very poor

indicators.note: off says a piece is removed from the word for just

parts.note: just means lawful, within the law
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (librum)

explanation.surface: Someone is told simply to take a pound off a pair of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers, but here it is British slang for dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British terms of disapproval meaning dreadful or of very poor quality.

clue.text: Scrabble broken up by unknown author's strict rules

indicators.note: broken up by says the first word is split open with the second placed inside it

parts.note: to scrabble is to scratch or claw
anon. marks the work of an unknown author

explanation.surface: A game of Scrabble is interrupted by some anonymous writer's rigid regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrabble' is not the board game but a verb meaning to scratch, and 'unknown author' is the abbreviation printed on anonymous works.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastical law is a body of formal church regulations, laid down strictly.

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a rating in the navy
a lush is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A sailor is described as intoxicated and muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is a noun here, a drunkard, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flushed red with embarrassment is flustered, so blushing stands in for confused.

definitions.meaning: when we pay for everyone, we say the bill is covered by us
a duty or burden that falls on someone

explanation.surface: Paying for the outing is presented as both a treat and a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a phrase for paying; as one it is a burden or obligation.

indicators.note: ignore says the letters for flash are dropped from the words that follow

parts.note: these words are the fodder the flash is taken from; that the rest runs on unbroken is a coincidence of the deletion, not a hidden-word device
a mo, a moment, is a flash

explanation.surface: Someone is told to disregard a flashing modem light and phone instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flash' looks like a modem's light; it is MO, a moment, removed from MODEM AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A call can be a requirement or request, as in the many calls on one's time.

parts.note: stoned suggests 'high', and college fellows dine at a raised table in hall

explanation.surface: A picture of intoxicated university lecturers at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' means high on drugs, but the table is high because it stands on a dais.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge colleges the fellows eat at a raised table at the end of the hall.

clue.text: Part of outfit in which hot musician plays?

definitions.text: Part of outfit in which hot musician plays?

parts.words: Part of outfit in which hot musician plays?
parts.note: a hot musician sweats, and the group he plays in is a band, so it reads as a band of sweaty players

explanation.surface: Asks which group a sizzling jazz player performs with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' suggests a band, but it is clothing; the item worn absorbs perspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A headband or wristband soaks up perspiration and is worn as part of sports kit.

clue.text: Sounds like leakier source of ink

indicators.note: sounds like says the word for leakier is to be said aloud

parts.note: something leakier is seepier

explanation.surface: A pen or pot that leaks more is presented as the ink's origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the cuttlefish, whose secretion gave the brown pigment used as ink.

clue.text: Not melodic, lacking time, key and bar

indicators.note: lacking says the letters for time and key are missing from the longer word

parts.note: something not melodic is tuneless
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A tuneless tune, missing its timing and key, played in a bar of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks musical but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: As prepositions, bar and this conjunction both express exception: everyone bar you, except if.

clue.text: Far-flung kudos right for anyone's puzzle

indicators.note: far-flung suggests the letters of kudos thrown about

parts.note: U is the British film certificate saying a film is suitable for anyone

explanation.surface: Widely spread praise for a puzzle that suits everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the universal film rating in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The number-placing grid game from Japan is a type of logic puzzle.

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters of the following words come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone is tanned yet surprisingly pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in the sun is how one acquires a tan, so the verb tan matches.

definitions.meaning: a worn bonnet is a hat that has seen better days

explanation.surface: A worn, unfashionable bonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something stale and familiar; literally it is a worn piece of headgear.

definitions.meaning: a colloquial contraction of 'it is not', as in dialect speech

explanation.surface: A slangy denial that something is corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' signals colloquial speech: 'it isn't' becomes 'tain't.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as slang it contracts 'it is not'; as a verb it means to spoil or contaminate morally.

clue.text: Target part of cereal to make sweet

parts.note: an end is an aim or target
an ear is the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant

explanation.surface: Aiming at a cereal ingredient to sweeten breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' means charming or dear, not sugary.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone dear or lovable, sweet in the affectionate sense.

clue.text: Traditional taste of Monbazillac is Salciccia knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back says the hidden letters are read backwards
a taste of something is just a small sample, so only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wine and Italian sausage pairing, drunk down, gives a traditional flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Traditional taste' as definition, but 'taste of' is the signal to take a sample of the wine and sausage names, and 'Traditional' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical means established and traditional in style, as in classical architecture.

parts.note: the law is slang for the police

explanation.surface: A policewoman goes over to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defect' looks like a verb, to change sides, but is the noun meaning fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaw is a fault or imperfection, a noun synonym for defect.

clue.text: Cold joint plus seconds comprising accompaniment to 24

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A cold cut of meat with second helpings, served alongside a main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is FISH DISH; fish and chips is the classic British pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried potato strips are the traditional British side served with fried fish.

clue.text: Believe it's money in the bank

definitions.meaning: a balance held in one's account

explanation.surface: Assurance that the bank holds funds.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to accept as true; as a noun it is a positive balance in an account.

definitions.meaning: a legal paper setting out wishes
a bequest is a giving away by someone who has died

explanation.surface: A document that betrays its secret at a glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a legal document by which the deceased gives property away.

indicators.note: in error says the letters of the preceding words are mistakenly arranged

explanation.surface: An airline has accidentally erased a customer's PIN.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airline' looks like a carrier, but is literally a line for air.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the tube carrying breath to the lungs, a passage for air.

clue.text: Unknown in City to quit permissible working

indicators.note: to quit says those letters leave the longer word

parts.note: something excusable is forgivable, permissible

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the City's letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
X is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An unknown figure in the City leaves a permitted job.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode letters the clue uses; 'working' is the definition, meaning in working order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in working order can be used, so the adjective fits operational.

clue.text: Function for which Antipodean delivers apiary?

indicators.note: an Australian or New Zealander delivering a word says it in that accent

parts.note: an apiary is where bees are kept, a beehive

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about why an Australian delivers bee colonies.
explanation.walkthrough: In a broad Antipodean accent 'beehive' comes out close to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that functions properly is said to work or perform correctly, as in behaving well.

indicators.note: sporadically means only every other letter is used

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the famous crooner

explanation.surface: A guitarist strums occasionally beside a singer's voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipes' looks like a singer's voice; it is the definition, meaning tubes.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of hollow tubes or conduits collectively, the material of pipework.

indicators.note: rewound tape runs backwards, so the word for tape is reversed

parts.note: to dub is to record onto tape

indicators.note: back-to-front says the back letter of had moves to the front

explanation.surface: A rewound cassette had its leader tape reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front' moves the last letter of HAD to the front, giving DHA. 'leader' looks like the start of a tape; it is a religious leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enlightened One founded and led Buddhism, a spiritual leader.

clue.text: Roles reversed in second part of 'Crime and Punishment'

indicators.note: reversed says the word for roles is written backwards

parts.note: roles in a play are parts

explanation.surface: The cast swaps roles in a staging of Dostoevsky's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the word 'Punishment', the second part of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather belt used for flogging is an instrument of corporal punishment.

parts.note: the main is the sea, so a course from the main is seafood

explanation.surface: A menu's principal dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate of seafood comes from the ocean, which old poetry calls the main.

explanation.surface: An American's plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a haul of loot; as a verb it means to pull or tug.

indicators.note: bound says the word duty encloses the record

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A junior's record of being dutiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty-bound' reads as one phrase, but 'bound' means surrounding EP.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command acts under a superior, a subordinate.

clue.text: For example holding five volts will make you smart

indicators.note: holding says the first word contains the others

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example
V is the Roman numeral for five
V is the symbol for volts

explanation.surface: A tip that five volts of electricity will sharpen you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shrewd and knowing is being clever, smart in the sense of quick-witted.

clue.text: Pushy me's taken 'a la Spooner' side dish for 24

indicators.note: a la Spooner says the first sounds of the two words are swapped, after Rev. Spooner

explanation.surface: A self-assertive person has been tricked in the style of Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the P and M sounds turns 'pushy me's' into the side dish; 24 across is FISH DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed marrowfat peas are a classic British side served with fish and chips.
